source.title: Emergent Semantic Role Understanding in Language Models

record.tranche_reason: Tests indirect evidence about how semantic-role representations are distributed in language models using probing, activation analyses, and ablations, rather than the toy-model superposition method.
record.gate_note: The study does not manipulate feature sparsity or importance, count features relative to dimensions, or test superposition or SAE recovery. PCA/t-SNE visualizations report partial role organization, and role-neuron and component ablations report causal effects. The random-neuron controls are reported as controls; cited results from other work are not recorded.
record.test_reason: This is a semantic-role probing and ablation study. It cites Toy Models of Superposition only in related work. It never measures superposition, feature-vs-dimension capacity, polysemanticity, SAE recovery or feature dimensionality. Its 'distributed' language rests on PCA 2-component variance, co-activation among selected role neurons, and counts of components needed for 80% of causal importance. None of these measures how many neurons a feature is spread across, so they do not test V4 as stated.
record.authors_conclusion: The paraphrase is mostly right. The authors' central conclusion is about emergence: pre-training contributes 12–19 F1 above a random baseline. Fine-tuning's added contribution grows with scale, so the emergence score falls. Role-selective neurons exist; Time neurons are causal at all scales, while Agent neurons shift from causal to interfering as scale grows. Implementation becomes more distributed with scale.
record.recipe_differences: Uses QA-SRL probes, PCA/t-SNE, neuron and component ablations, and co-activation analysis; it does not use the toy-model superposition setup or test feature sparsity and geometry.
record.method_sensitivity: Model scale changes the reported role organization and ablation effects. For role ablations, custom models use retrain ablation while GPT-2 and Pythia use no-retrain ablation.

fits_no_version.finding: Final-layer 2-PC variance falls with scale (19.2%, 14.8%, 10.1%, 7.3%). Role-selective neurons co-activate weakly more within role than across role (0.24 vs 0.10).
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Semantic-role structure in activations is partial and becomes less captured by low-dimensional projections as model scale grows.

fits_no_version.finding: Agent-neuron ablation hurts small models but helps larger ones; Time-neuron ablation hurts at all custom scales. Random-neuron controls are near zero on GPT-2 and Pythia.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: The causal contribution of semantic-role-selective neurons changes with model scale.

fits_no_version.finding: The number of components needed for 80% of Agent-F1 causal importance grows with scale, and the concentration ratio falls from 58% to 44%.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Causal importance for semantic roles spreads across more layers and components at larger scale.

record.code_released: Code and trained model weights available from the authors upon request; no URL stated
record.problems: Custom-model role-conditioned and overall ablation results are single-seed point estimates. Role visualizations are descriptive, with low variance explained by the first two PCs and partial clustering. Custom models are small and trained on WikiText-103; the paper notes that GPT-2 and Pythia remain small relative to massive commercial LLMs. GPT-2/Pythia ablations use a different protocol from the custom models.
record.rows_left_out: The study also reports overall-F1 role-conditioned ablations in Table 4, additional time and random-neuron control ablations in Tables 10–11, and layer-wise probe/CKA results. These were not extracted because they do not directly measure feature distribution, sparsity, or superposition for the claim versions.

untested.parts: No toy model, no sparsity sweep, no feature-count-vs-dimension geometry.
No test of capacity competition or of importance-driven dedicated vs shared dimensions.
No analysis of the causes of polysemanticity.
No measure of how many neurons a feature is spread across, and no SAE recovery. The 'distributed' claims rest on PCA variance, co-activation and component counts.

record.verdict_notes: The record's V4 link is the borderline call. The authors use 'distributed, overlapping representations' loosely, but no measurement addresses neuron-level spread of a feature or dictionary recovery. The study also identifies highly selective single neurons (Table 9), which, if anything, points toward monosemantic-looking units rather than superposition. Custom-model ablations are single-seed.

versions.untested_parts: No toy-model superposition, sparse-feature sweep, geometry transition, or feature-count-versus-dimension test.
Does not test whether polysemanticity results from capacity competition or whether importance determines dedicated versus shared dimensions.
Does not test polysemanticity as an alternative explanation or whether it is evidence for superposition.

Examines semantic-role organization, not a broad inventory of model features; does not test SAE recovery or large commercial models. The neuron-ablation replications on GPT-2 and Pythia do not directly measure feature distribution across neurons.
No SAE features, or tests of their completeness, stability, or canonical status.
PCA visualizations do not test whether superposed features are one-dimensional directions or multidimensional features.

rows.subject: Tiny (0.4M)
rows.stage_stated: trained from scratch on WikiText-103; pre-trained
rows.operation_detail: PCA visualization of final-layer activations by PropBank role
rows.measure: Variance explained by first two principal components; role organization
rows.value: 19.2% of variance; ARG0-Agent shows some separation
rows.note: The text describes some separation, not complete clustering.
rows.check: Variance explained by the first two PCs of final-layer activations is not a measure of features spread across neurons. A low 2-PC share is compatible with many non-superposed representations.

rows.subject: Medium (56.7M)

rows.subject: Custom models (Tiny, Small, Base, Medium; aggregate)
rows.operation_detail: Pairwise Pearson correlations among PCA-identified role-selective neurons
rows.measure: Mean within-role and across-role correlation
rows.value: within-role correlation approximately 0.24; distributions heavily overlap
rows.uncertainty: standard deviations approximately 0.3–0.4; Figure 5 reports means 0.23 and 0.11
rows.note: Authors describe role-specific grouping as weak but present, and interpret it as consistent with distributed, overlapping representations.
rows.check: These are correlations among PCA-selected role neurons (within 0.24 vs across 0.10). They show weak functional grouping, not how many neurons a feature is spread across, and not superposition.

source_check.scope: Only the listed rows, labels and statements were checked; presence is not whole-study approval.

reader_labels.label: supports
reader_labels.condition: Custom models, final-layer PropBank role visualizations and role-selective-neuron correlations
reader_labels.reason: The representations show partial role organization, low variance captured by the first two PCs, and weak but higher within-role than across-role correlations, consistent with distributed role representations (r1–r5).

reader_labels.label: limits_scope
reader_labels.condition: Custom models, role visualization and correlation analyses
reader_labels.reason: Role separation is partial and the correlation distributions heavily overlap; this is indirect evidence about selected semantic roles, not a general test of feature distribution or SAE recovery (r1–r5).
